questions.q: Why doesn't print() work well for a script that runs on an unattended schedule?
options: Its output disappears when the process exits, leaving no record to check after the fact
Scheduled scripts are not allowed to call print() at all
print() is slower than logging for every use case
print() cannot output strings, only numbers
questions.explain: Without a terminal open to watch, print() output is simply lost — logging can persist it to a file.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a logging level like INFO, WARNING, or ERROR?
options: It controls how fast the script runs
It determines which Python version is required
It filters which messages actually get shown or saved, without deleting any logging calls from the code
It only affects messages sent to a file, never the console
questions.explain: Setting the configured level to INFO means debug() calls are skipped while info() and above still appear.

questions.q: What does logger.exception() add compared to logger.error()?
options: Nothing — they are exactly identical in every case
It silently suppresses the exception instead of logging it
The full traceback of the exception, in addition to the error message
It automatically retries the failed operation
questions.explain: logger.exception() is designed to be called from inside an except block to capture the full traceback.

questions.q: What does a logging Handler control?
options: Where a log message is sent, such as the console or a file
Which level of message severity exists
The Python version the script requires
How many times a function is called
questions.explain: A FileHandler sends messages to a file; a StreamHandler sends them to the console. You can use both at once.

questions.q: Why pass logger.info("Extracted %d rows", len(rows)) instead of an f-string?
options: The string formatting only happens if the message will actually be logged, which logging's %-style arguments allow
f-strings are not valid Python syntax inside a logging call
It changes the logging level automatically
It is required by the FileHandler class
questions.explain: logging defers formatting until it knows the message will be emitted, which an f-string would do eagerly regardless.
